title: Having Beer after Prayer? Measuring Cultural Bias in Large Language Models
findings: Large Language Models, including those specifically trained on Arabic, exhibit a bias towards Western culture and fail at appropriate cultural adaptation in Arabic. A key example is LMs suggesting alcoholic beverages even when the prompt explicitly mentions Islamic prayer. Models also struggled with entities related to religious places of worship (mosques vs. churches), showing cultural unfairness and an inability to adapt to the specific religious context of the prompts.

measurement_description: The benchmark, CAMEL, measures cultural bias in Large Language Models by evaluating their performance on culturally-invoking prompts in Arabic. Specifically for religion, it measures the models' ability to provide culturally and religiously appropriate completions for prompts related to Islamic practices (e.g., prayer) and places of worship (e.g., mosques), contrasting these with Western cultural norms.
